case.case_title: Sasanasiritissa Thero and Others v. P.A. De Silva, Chief Inspector, C.I.D. and Others
case.source_citation: Sri Lanka Law Reports (1989) 2 Sri LR 356

clause.text: No citizen shall be discriminated against on the grounds of race, religion, language, caste, sex, political opinion, place of birth or any one of such grounds.

case_context.legal_issue: Whether the petitioners were discriminated against on the ground of political opinion in violation of Article 12(2).
case_context.petitioner_claim: The petitioners alleged their arrest and detention were politically motivated and thus discriminatory under Article 12(2).
case_context.respondent_argument: Respondents denied political motivation and argued no discrimination was established due to lack of evidence.
key_facts: The 1st petitioner was a political opponent and patron of the Sri Lanka Freedom Party.
The petitioners were arrested following a bomb explosion but no credible evidence linked them to the incident.
Allegations of political victimization were made but not supported by admissible evidence.
The Court found the allegations against the 5th and 6th respondents of political instigation were unproven.

reasoning.interpretation_summary: Article 12(2) prohibits discrimination on political opinion. The Court required cogent evidence to establish political victimization and discrimination.
reasoning.application_to_facts: The Court found the petitioners failed to prove political discrimination as the allegations were vague, uncorroborated, and based on belief rather than evidence. Therefore, no violation of Article 12(2) was established.
principles_established: Allegations of political discrimination must be strictly proved by cogent evidence.
Bare assertions or vague allegations are insufficient to establish discrimination.
The Court will dismiss claims of discrimination lacking admissible evidence.
precedents_cited: Kottunnage Somaratne Ranasinghe v. Ceylon Plywood Corporation
Gunasena Thenabadu v. University of Ceylon

outcome.holding: The Court held that the petitioners did not establish discrimination on the ground of political opinion under Article 12(2). The allegations against the 5th and 6th respondents were dismissed.

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: Article 12(2) was materially engaged as the petitioners claimed political discrimination, but the Court found no sufficient evidence to uphold this claim, affecting the outcome against certain respondents.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: The Court held that the allegations of political victimization against the 5th and 6th respondents were vague, uncorroborated, and not established by admissible evidence, thus no violation of Article 12(2).
